method: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses; least inconsistent, never most supported

hypotheses.title: ICE contract design and monitoring may insulate GEO operations from proportional financial consequences
The oversight episodes are separate incidents handled through ordinary remedies and readiness purchasing

new_assessments.reason: The nonfinal Novoa partial-liability finding contains no ICE responsibility, CPARS, deduction, option, or acquisition decision record.
GEO wage discretion is legally material but does not disclose any ICE contract consequence or procurement response.
The stay posture explains procedural delay but does not establish how ICE treated the case in contract administration.

interpretation: Adding the corrected Novoa legal findings increases the evaluated denominator but adds no discriminatory contract-consequence evidence. Hypothesis 335 remains narrowly least inconsistent because the prior Folkston and Northwest consequence records are more diagnostic than the litigation postures. This ranking is not confirmation. South Texas, Golden State, vendor-paid overtime, later no-findings, and ordinary capacity/readiness explanations preserve meaningful support for H0 336.
prohibited_inference: Neither the ACH ranking nor later award-action continuity establishes favoritism, political influence, litigation causation, or an ICE decision to disregard any ruling.
